findings.description: Without jq, the rules run on the raw one-line JSON payload. There the command always ends in a `"`, so the two rules anchored on the end of the command never match: the push-to-trunk block (line 62) and the bare-push-on-trunk block (line 68) both let the push through. Quote: `COMMAND=$INPUT`.
findings.body:
**Without jq, git-safety's two trunk rules now silently let the push through.**

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/7f07fccaba12436cea9a529ba2c20ab01db4e443/.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh#L8-L18

```bash
else
  # The raw payload still carries the command's words for the checks below.
  COMMAND=$INPUT
fi
```

The comment holds for the unanchored rules (`rm -rf`, `--force`/`-f\b`, `reset --hard\b`, `checkout -b\b`). It does not hold for the two trunk rules, which need the command to end:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/claude-code-config/blob/7f07fccaba12436cea9a529ba2c20ab01db4e443/.claude/hooks/git-safety.sh#L58-L72

- **Push to trunk, line 62:** the regex ends `${TRUNK}([[:space:]]|\$|[|&;])`. Claude Code sends one-line JSON, e.g. `..."command":"git push origin main","description":"Push branch"}}`. After `main` comes `"`, which none of the alternatives accept, so `git push origin main`, `HEAD:main` and `refs/heads/main` pass. It only matches by accident, when a later field happens to hold `main` followed by a blank.
- **Bare push on trunk, line 68:** `git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]*$` can never match, because `push` is always followed by `"` and more JSON.

Before this delta a missing jq failed closed (the prior round's important); now it fails open for exactly the rules this hook exists for. `push-gate.sh` still prompts the user (its `^...$` `CANONICAL` regex can't match a payload starting with `{`, so it asks), and `scripts/pre-push` has no trunk check, so a click is all that stands between the agent and a trunk push.

Same root cause, other sites:
- JSON escapes stay undecoded: a tab is the two characters `\t`, so `rm -rf<TAB>x`, `git<TAB>push --force` and `git reset<TAB>--hard` block with jq and pass without it.
- The rules also scan `description`, `cwd` and later fields, so a description like "clean up (rm -rf build)" blocks a harmless command.
- The `[ -z "$COMMAND" ]` branch can no longer fire.

`tests/hooks/git-safety.test.sh` covers only force-push and `ls -la` without jq, which is why this passes.

**Fix:** decode before matching, as `push-gate.sh` does, and end the command where its JSON string ends (e.g. turn `\"` into `'`, `\n`/`\t` into a blank or newline, and each remaining `"` into a newline, so `$` and the trunk terminator hold). Or, without jq, block any payload naming both `git` and `push`. Add a no-jq `git push origin main` case on trunk to the shell harness.

findings.description: The `BLOCKED: git-safety could not read the hook payload.` message is never asserted: `expect` sends stderr to /dev/null and checks only the exit code, and the Rust `tools/hooks-rs/tests/git_safety.rs:129` case checks only exit 2. Rewording or dropping the message leaves both suites green; capture stderr in the `not json` case and add a Rust test asserting `stderr.contains("could not read the hook payload")`.

The `not json` case runs with the caller's `$PATH`, so on a machine without jq the hook takes the no-jq branch, treats `not json` as the command, exits 0 and the case fails. Run it with a PATH that holds a jq link, or skip it when `command -v jq` fails.

The new tests do not cover three paths the recursive `realpath` handles: a chained link (a link to a link into the freeze), an absolute link target, and a `..` after a symlinked directory. The code traces correctly; a chained-link case (e.g. `hop.ts -> alias.ts`, reusing the existing alias fixture) would also pin that the budget is spent per hop.

PR body, Evidence: "63 passed (frozen_paths 27, git_safety 14, path_guards 14, tool_result_size 8)" is stale after this push, which adds five tests; the counts are now 68 (frozen_paths 29, git_safety 14, path_guards 16, tool_result_size 9).

PR body, Merge Danger: "The one behaviour change today is `git-safety.sh` blocking on an unparseable payload" (and the summary's `# blocks when the payload does not parse`) no longer covers the change: `git-safety.sh` now also falls back to matching the raw payload when jq is missing. Name that fallback in the body.
